info.title: Data Hub MCP
info.description: Model Context Protocol server for Data Hub. Authenticate with an OAuth / Bearer access token (`Authorization: Bearer …`). The transport requires the `read` scope; mutating tools additionally require `write`, except `send_feedback`, which any read token can call.

tools.name: list_instruments
tools.title: List Instruments
tools.description: List all registered lab instruments with run counts, the instrument's connection (whether new files can reach Data Hub, and why not), its one active watcher (host, folder, file patterns, upload mode, settings state), and how many past watchers it has had. Optionally filter by status. watcherCount, watchersOnline, hasDeregisteredWatcher, lastWatcherHeartbeatAt, activeWatcherId and the top-level filePatterns are deprecated: use watcher and connection.

version.description: Installed watcher version. Null until its first heartbeat.

status.description: Detailed watcher status. `stale` means no heartbeat for 5 minutes, or no return from a restart within 15.

statusReason.description: Why the watcher is waiting (the missing folder), or why it stopped for a restart (`system_shutdown` or `auto_update`). The reason stays while the status reads `stale`.

filePatterns.description: File patterns from the watcher's config, in config order.

configState.description: State of the watcher's settings: `pending` (a change is waiting for the watcher), `rejected` (the watcher refused the latest change), `edited_on_pc` (a PC edit takes effect when the watcher restarts), `applied`, or `none`.

sharedComputerWith.description: Other instruments whose active watchers run on the same computer (hostnames compared without case).

watcher.description: The instrument's one active watcher, or null when it has none. Replaces watcherCount, watchersOnline and the activeWatcher* fields.

reason.description: Why the instrument is offline. Null in every other state.

connection.description: Whether new files can reach Data Hub. `online`: the watcher checked in within 5 minutes. `restarting`: the watcher stopped for a Windows restart or an automatic update less than 15 minutes ago. `connecting`: the watcher registered and hasn't sent a heartbeat yet, for up to 15 minutes after it registered or the instrument was confirmed; after that the instrument is `offline` with reason `never_checked_in`. `offline`: anything else. This does not take the instrument's status into account: a pending instrument can be `online`.

pastWatcherCount.description: How many deregistered watchers the instrument has had.

filePatterns.description: Deprecated. Use `watcher.filePatterns`, which keeps the config's order. This list is de-duplicated and sorted.

activeWatcherId.description: Deprecated. Use `watcher.id`. This also names the most recently deregistered watcher when none is active.

watcherCount.description: Deprecated. An instrument has at most one watcher. Use `watcher`.

tools.name: get_instrument
tools.title: Get Instrument
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific instrument: its connection (online, restarting, connecting or offline, with the reason when offline), its one active watcher (host, OS, version, folder, file patterns, upload mode, settings state, other instruments on the same computer), and how many past watchers it has had. watcherCount, watchersOnline, watchersOffline, lastWatcherHeartbeatAt, the activeWatcher* fields and the top-level filePatterns are deprecated: use watcher and connection.

version.description: Installed watcher version. Null until its first heartbeat.

status.description: Detailed watcher status. `stale` means no heartbeat for 5 minutes, or no return from a restart within 15.

statusReason.description: Why the watcher is waiting (the missing folder), or why it stopped for a restart (`system_shutdown` or `auto_update`). The reason stays while the status reads `stale`.

filePatterns.description: File patterns from the watcher's config, in config order.

configState.description: State of the watcher's settings: `pending` (a change is waiting for the watcher), `rejected` (the watcher refused the latest change), `edited_on_pc` (a PC edit takes effect when the watcher restarts), `applied`, or `none`.

sharedComputerWith.description: Other instruments whose active watchers run on the same computer (hostnames compared without case).

watcher.description: The instrument's one active watcher, or null when it has none. Replaces watcherCount, watchersOnline and the activeWatcher* fields.

reason.description: Why the instrument is offline. Null in every other state.

connection.description: Whether new files can reach Data Hub. `online`: the watcher checked in within 5 minutes. `restarting`: the watcher stopped for a Windows restart or an automatic update less than 15 minutes ago. `connecting`: the watcher registered and hasn't sent a heartbeat yet, for up to 15 minutes after it registered or the instrument was confirmed; after that the instrument is `offline` with reason `never_checked_in`. `offline`: anything else. This does not take the instrument's status into account: a pending instrument can be `online`.

pastWatcherCount.description: How many deregistered watchers the instrument has had.

filePatterns.description: Deprecated. Use `watcher.filePatterns`, which keeps the config's order. This list is de-duplicated and sorted.

watcherCount.description: Deprecated. An instrument has at most one watcher. Use `watcher`.

activeWatcherId.description: Deprecated. Use `watcher.id`. This also names the most recently deregistered watcher when none is active.

tools.name: get_instrument_filter_options
tools.title: Get Instrument Filter Options
tools.description: Return the valid search_runs metadata filter values for one instrument (wavelengths, dye channels, etc.). Prefer the datahub://instruments/{id}/filter-options resource when the client supports resources.

tools.name: search_runs
tools.title: Search Runs
tools.description: Search instrument runs with filtering, pagination, and sorting. Each run lists its lab notebooks. Supports run status, lab notebook, and instrument-metadata filters (plate reader, gel-doc, qPCR, Hina microscope, Epson scanner, Aunty). Prefer global_search when the query may match filenames, instrument names, or attributor names rather than run IDs. Discover valid metadata filter values via get_instrument_filter_options or datahub://instruments/{id}/filter-options.

instrumentId.description: Filter to one or more instrument IDs

search.description: Search text matched against run ID only

dateFrom.description: Start date (inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD). Day boundary is UTC, not the viewer's timezone.

dateTo.description: End date (inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD). Day boundary is UTC, not the viewer's timezone.

sort.description: Sort field (default: acquired_at — when the run started on the instrument PC, falling back to created_at). updated_at is the last change to the run or any of its files.

measurementMode.description: Plate reader: filter by measurement mode

measurementType.description: Plate reader: filter by measurement type

hinaChannel.description: Hina microscope: filter by channel name

hinaSize.description: Hina microscope: filter by sizes JSON object string (from filter-options)

colorMode.description: Epson scanner: filter by color mode (e.g. 'rgb', 'bw')

auntyExperimentType.description: Aunty: filter by experiment type (thermal_ramp, sizing, isothermal). Mixed workbooks match if they include the type.

auntyTemperature.description: Aunty: filter by a start/end pair (e.g. '25|95') or a hold temperature (e.g. '25').

auntyRampRate.description: Aunty: filter by ramp rate in °C/min (e.g. '1')

ranBy.description: Filter by attributor. Pass a user id, the literal "me" for the authenticated token owner, or "unattributed" for runs with no attributions. Use get_me for your user id, or list_run_attributors to discover colleagues.

hasLabNotebook.description: true: only runs in at least one lab notebook. false: only runs in none. Deleted lab notebooks don't count.

labNotebookId.description: Only runs in this lab notebook, on any instrument. Find the id with list_lab_notebooks. Works for a deleted lab notebook too.

status.description: Filter by derived run status (OR'd together). Status is derived from a run's raw file states, priority-exclusive: failed (any file failed processing), stalled (a file has been in processing past the stall window and can be reprocessed), upload_failed (the watcher gave up on a file, for example because it's no longer on the instrument PC), waiting_upload (files requested, or ones the watcher uploads on its own), uploaded, queued (reprocessing files waiting for a free processing slot), processing (in flight), not_uploaded (files only on the instrument PC that nobody requested), completed (all done), empty (no files). The deprecated pending means waiting_upload or not_uploaded.

tools.name: get_run
tools.title: Get Run
tools.description: Get details for a specific instrument run by its natural key (instrument ID + run ID). Returns metadata, timestamps, instrument info, attributions, and lab notebooks by default. Pass include to attach the first page of files, comments, and/or a failure_summary without extra tool calls. To show the interactive report (plate maps, spectra, images) or a bounded processed-CSV sample, call get_run_report for the same run.

include.description: Optional extras. "attributions" is accepted but redundant — attributions are always included. "files" returns the first page (50) via list_run_files shape.

tools.name: get_run_report
tools.title: Get Run Report
tools.description: Return an analysis-ready summary for a run: file counts, failure summary, image/report file refs, and a bounded processed-CSV sample (columns + first rows). Prefer this over downloading full CSVs when comparing or summarizing experimental results. Hosts that support MCP Apps render the interactive report View when this tool is called.

tools.name: list_run_files
tools.title: List Run Files
tools.description: List files associated with a run (raw uploads and processed artifacts) with their status, category, and size. Paginated — runs can have thousands of files. Deleted files are left out unless includeDeleted is true; each deleted file has deletedAt and who deleted it, and restore_files brings it back. Filter by status to gather fileIds for request_run_upload (e.g. status=['detected', 'upload_failed']). An upload_failed file is one the watcher gave up on; its errorMessage and uploadFailureReason say why. Use get_file for full per-file detail including metadata and S3 location.

status.description: Filter to one or more file statuses (OR'd). 'queued' files are waiting for a free processing slot after a reprocess request. Omit to return all statuses.

tools.name: claim_run
tools.title: Claim Run
tools.description: Mark a run as performed by the authenticated user. Idempotent — claiming a run you already claimed is a no-op. Only self-attribution is supported; you cannot claim a run on behalf of another user. Prefer claim_runs when attributing multiple runs.

tools.name: claim_runs
tools.title: Claim Runs
tools.description: Mark multiple runs on one instrument as performed by the authenticated user (max 100). Idempotent per run. Returns claimed runs and any runIds that were not found; a missing ID does not fail the whole batch. Only self-attribution is supported.

tools.name: unclaim_run
tools.title: Unclaim Run
tools.description: Remove the authenticated user's attribution from a run. Idempotent — unclaiming a run you don't currently claim is a no-op. Only self-attribution is supported; you cannot remove another user's attribution.

tools.name: list_run_attributors
tools.title: List Run Attributors
tools.description: List distinct users who have claimed at least one run on a given instrument. Use the returned userId with search_runs ranBy=<userId>.

tools.name: list_run_comments
tools.title: List Run Comments
tools.description: List comments on a run (oldest first), including author display info.

tools.name: add_run_comment
tools.title: Add Run Comment
tools.description: Add a comment on a run as the authenticated user. Author is taken from the token — you cannot comment as another user.

tools.name: edit_run_comment
tools.title: Edit Run Comment
tools.description: Edit one of your own comments. Returns an error if the comment is missing or authored by someone else.

tools.name: delete_run_comment
tools.title: Delete Run Comment
tools.description: Soft-delete a comment. You can delete your own comments; workspace admins can delete any comment. Idempotent if already deleted.

tools.name: reprocess_run
tools.title: Reprocess Run
tools.description: Re-run Lambda processing for every uploaded, completed, failed, or stalled raw file on a run. Processed artifacts are skipped. The instrument must have a Lambda processor. Each file starts as soon as a processing slot is free (at most 10 raw files process at once across Data Hub by default), and a file that does not start right away waits with status 'queued'. filesQueued counts every file accepted, whether it started or is waiting. Prefer this over looping reprocess_file for bulk retries after a parser fix, to kick stuck uploads, or to recover files that never reported back from processing.

tools.name: cancel_queued_files
tools.title: Cancel Queued Files
tools.description: Take every queued file of a run out of the reprocessing queue. Each one becomes 'failed' with a message that says the reprocess was cancelled, and can be reprocessed again. Files that have already started processing are not affected. Use it when queued files are not going to start, or after a reprocess_run that was a mistake. filesCancelled is 0 when the run has no queued files. Works on a soft-deleted run too.

tools.name: delete_run
tools.title: Delete Run
tools.description: Soft-delete a run (sets deleted_at). Does not remove files or S3 objects. Also cancels the uploads requested for the run's files: they go back to 'detected' and leave the watcher's queue. Use restore_run to undo the delete; it does not bring the upload requests back. Idempotent: deleting an already-deleted run succeeds as a no-op.

tools.name: restore_run
tools.title: Restore Run
tools.description: Restore a soft-deleted run by clearing deleted_at. Does not bring back upload requests that the delete cancelled; request them again. Idempotent: restoring a run that is not deleted succeeds as a no-op.

tools.name: request_run_upload
tools.title: Request Run Upload
tools.description: Queue specific detected or upload_failed files for watcher upload (max 100). Requires an instrument whose watcher is online or restarting; a request made during a restart waits until the watcher is back. Offline, connecting, pending and retired instruments are refused. Idempotent for files already in upload_requested. An upload_failed file's errorMessage says why the last request failed (often a folder renamed on the PC); requesting it again before that is fixed fails the same way.

tools.name: request_run_upload_all
tools.title: Request Run Upload All
tools.description: Queue every detected and upload_failed file on a run for watcher upload. Requires an instrument whose watcher is online or restarting; a request made during a restart waits until the watcher is back. Offline, connecting, pending and retired instruments are refused.

tools.name: list_lab_notebooks
tools.title: List Lab Notebooks
tools.description: List lab notebooks. A lab notebook is one page (Notion, Google Docs, or any http or https page) with a name, and it can hold runs from any instrument. Search by name, description, or a pasted link; a link finds only the lab notebook for that page. Each lab notebook has its run count, instrument count, and last run. List a lab notebook's runs with search_runs labNotebookId.

query.description: A name, part of a description, or a pasted lab notebook link

ownerId.description: Only lab notebooks owned by this user: a user id, or "me" for the signed-in user

sort.description: Sort field (default: last_run, when the lab notebook's newest run started)

order.description: Sort order (default: asc for name, desc for the rest)

tools.name: get_lab_notebook
tools.title: Get Lab Notebook
tools.description: Get one lab notebook by id: its page link, name, description, owner, run count, instrument count, last run, and who created, changed, or deleted it. Deleted lab notebooks are returned too, with deleted_at set. List its runs with search_runs labNotebookId.

labNotebookId.description: The lab notebook's id, from list_lab_notebooks or a run's lab notebooks

tools.name: create_lab_notebook
tools.title: Create Lab Notebook
tools.description: Create a lab notebook for one page, and optionally add up to 100 runs from one instrument to it. Each page can have only one lab notebook, deleted ones included. If the page already has one, this fails with that lab notebook's id: add runs to it with add_runs_to_lab_notebook instead, after restore_lab_notebook when it is deleted. Search first with list_lab_notebooks and the link when unsure. The owner stays empty unless you pass ownerId. Acts as the signed-in user. Adding runs doesn't record who ran them; call claim_runs for that.

url.description: The lab notebook page's http or https URL

name.description: The lab notebook's name, usually the page's title

ownerId.description: The person responsible for the lab notebook: a user id, or "me" for the signed-in user. Leave out for no owner. global_search with scope users finds a colleague's id.

instrumentId.description: Instrument of the runs to add. Required with runIds.

tools.name: update_lab_notebook
tools.title: Update Lab Notebook
tools.description: Change a lab notebook's name, description, owner, or page link. Leave a field out to keep it; pass null for description or ownerId to clear it. A new link must point to a page no other lab notebook has. A deleted lab notebook can't change until it is restored.

labNotebookId.description: The lab notebook's id, from list_lab_notebooks or a run's lab notebooks

description.description: New description. Null or blank clears it.

ownerId.description: New owner: a user id, or "me" for the signed-in user. Null clears it.

url.description: New http or https URL for the page

tools.name: delete_lab_notebook
tools.title: Delete Lab Notebook
tools.description: Delete a lab notebook. Its runs stop listing it, but it keeps them, so restore_lab_notebook brings it back with the same runs. Confirm with the user first, and say how many runs it holds (run_count from get_lab_notebook).

labNotebookId.description: The lab notebook's id, from list_lab_notebooks or a run's lab notebooks

tools.name: restore_lab_notebook
tools.title: Restore Lab Notebook
tools.description: Bring back a deleted lab notebook with the runs it had. Find deleted lab notebooks with list_lab_notebooks includeDeleted.

labNotebookId.description: The lab notebook's id, from list_lab_notebooks or a run's lab notebooks

tools.name: add_runs_to_lab_notebook
tools.title: Add Runs to Lab Notebook
tools.description: Add up to 100 runs from one instrument to a lab notebook, and report an outcome for each. Runs already in it stay as they are, and deleted or missing runs are skipped. To link runs to a page, find its lab notebook with list_lab_notebooks and the link, or make one with create_lab_notebook. Acts as the signed-in user. Adding runs doesn't record who ran them; call claim_runs for that.

labNotebookId.description: The lab notebook's id, from list_lab_notebooks or a run's lab notebooks

tools.name: remove_runs_from_lab_notebook
tools.title: Remove Runs from Lab Notebook
tools.description: Remove up to 100 runs from one instrument from a lab notebook, and report an outcome for each. The lab notebook stays, even when it has no runs left.

labNotebookId.description: The lab notebook's id, from list_lab_notebooks or a run's lab notebooks

tools.name: report_view_items
tools.title: Report View Items
tools.description: Return a paginated window of run report items (images, PDFs, spectra, videos, or media) with download URLs. Used by the Data Hub run report view. Call `get_run_report` instead.

kind.description: Report item kind: image, media, pdf, spectrum, or video. `media` lists videos and images together, without the image that is a video's poster

anchor.description: File id to centre the window on; overrides offset when found

tools.name: report_view_file_url
tools.title: Report View File URL
tools.description: Return a short-lived download URL for one file on a run, found by numeric id or by filename suffix. The view reads CSV and JSON bodies from that URL itself. Used by the Data Hub run report view. Call `get_run_report` instead.

fileId.description: Numeric file ID. Takes precedence over `suffix`

suffix.description: Filename suffix to match instead of an id, e.g. _aunty_plate.json

tools.name: get_file
tools.title: Get File
tools.description: Get detailed metadata for a single file by its numeric ID, including status, S3 location, size, extracted metadata, and any error message. A deleted file is returned too: deletedAt is set, and deletedBy (a user ID) or deletedByToken names who deleted it.

tools.name: get_file_download_url
tools.title: Get File Download URL
tools.description: Get a short-lived pre-signed S3 URL to download the raw file contents. URL expires after 15 minutes. Also returns the file's run as `instrumentId` and `runId`. `unclaimed` is true when nobody has claimed the run yet. Then ask the user once whether they ran it, and call claim_run if they did.

tools.name: get_run_archive
tools.title: Get Run Archive
tools.description: Get a downloadable ZIP archive of every active, uploaded file in a run. If the archive is already cached, returns a short-lived (15 min) pre-signed S3 URL the caller can fetch directly without auth — paste it into a browser or share it as a download link. If the archive isn't cached, kicks off an async build and returns `{ status: 'building', jobId, retryAfterSeconds }`; call this tool again after the suggested wait to poll for completion. Most archives finish in a few seconds; large runs may take a minute or two. Mirrors the REST `download-archive` route, including its dedup-by-fingerprint cache, so concurrent callers share a single Lambda invocation. `unclaimed` is true when nobody has claimed the run yet. Then ask the user once whether they ran it, and call claim_run if they did.

tools.name: reprocess_file
tools.title: Reprocess File
tools.description: Re-run the Lambda processing workflow for an uploaded, failed, completed, or stalled raw file on an instrument that has a Lambda processor. A file is stalled when it has been in 'processing' longer than the configured stall window (20 minutes by default, past the Lambda's 15-minute limit) or has no processing-started timestamp. Processed artifacts are rejected. The file is queued first and starts as soon as a processing slot is free. The result is status 'processing' when the file started right away and 'queued' when it did not, for example because 10 raw files are already processing (the default limit across Data Hub). A file that is already 'queued' is rejected. Use this to retry after a parser fix, transient Lambda failure, a stuck upload that never entered processing, or a file that never reported back from processing.

tools.name: delete_files
tools.title: Delete Files
tools.description: Delete up to 100 files of one run, whether or not they were uploaded, and report a result for each. A deleted file is left out of the run's file lists and downloads, but stays in storage, records who deleted it, and can still be read by its ID; restore_files brings it back. Only the files you name are deleted unless includeLinked is true. includeLinked also deletes the files linked to them: for a raw file, the processed files made from it (such as its preview video and image), and the run.json saved with its capture when every raw file in that folder is being deleted. `linked` lists them. Before you pass includeLinked: true, tell the user it also deletes those linked files and get their OK. A file that is queued or processing is refused until processing finishes (a stalled file can be deleted), and so is any file of a deleted run. A refused file doesn't stop the others. Deleting a file that is already deleted succeeds with alreadyApplied. Acts as the signed-in user. Ask the user to confirm first.

fileIds.description: Numeric IDs of files in this run, from list_run_files (1–100). An ID that isn't a file of this run gets a 404 result.

includeLinked.description: Also delete the files linked to these: the processed files made from a raw file, and its run.json. Default false. Confirm with the user before you pass true.

tools.name: restore_files
tools.title: Restore Files
tools.description: Bring back up to 100 deleted files of one run, and report a result for each. Find deleted files with list_run_files includeDeleted. Only the files you name come back unless includeLinked is true. includeLinked also restores their deleted linked files: the deleted processed files made from a raw file, the raw file a deleted processed file was made from, and the run.json of a restored raw file's folder. `linked` lists each with its own result. Before you pass includeLinked: true, tell the user it also restores those linked files and get their OK. A file is refused with a 409 (details.reason path_in_use, and details.held_by naming the file) when another file of the run now has its name or path, and so is any file of a deleted run. A refused file doesn't stop the others. Restoring a file that isn't deleted succeeds with alreadyApplied. Acts as the signed-in user. Ask the user to confirm first.

fileIds.description: Numeric IDs of files in this run, from list_run_files (1–100). An ID that isn't a file of this run gets a 404 result.

includeLinked.description: Also restore the deleted files linked to these. Default false. Confirm with the user before you pass true.

tools.name: dismiss_file
tools.title: Dismiss File (Deprecated)
tools.description: Deprecated: use delete_files, which takes up to 100 files of a run, can delete their linked files too, and has restore_files to undo it. It still works, for one file by its ID, and will be removed. Soft-delete a file from a run, whether or not it has been uploaded. The file stays in storage and records who deleted it. It is refused while the file is queued or still processing (a stalled file can be deleted), and for a file of a deleted run. Idempotent: deleting an already-deleted file succeeds as a no-op. Deletes only that file, never its linked files.

tools.name: list_watchers
tools.title: List Watchers
tools.description: List watcher agents with effective status, hostname, instrument assignment, and last heartbeat. Optionally include deregistered watchers or filter by effective status.

instrumentId.description: Filter watchers to a specific instrument

status.description: Filter by effective status. stale is computed, never stored: a watching or waiting watcher with no heartbeat for 5 minutes, one that stopped for a restart or an automatic update and has sent none for 15 minutes, or a registered one with no first heartbeat 15 minutes after it registered or its instrument was confirmed (a pending instrument's watcher stays registered). A stopped watcher otherwise stays stopped, and a deregistered watcher is always stopped.

tools.name: get_watcher
tools.title: Get Watcher
tools.description: Get watcher detail including config YAML, OS info, effective status (with statusReason when waiting for a missing folder, when stopped for a Windows restart or shutdown (system_shutdown), or when stopped to install an automatic update (auto_update, which watcher 1.4.2 and later send); the reason stays while the status reads stale), config revision numbers, any pending config change, and deregistration actor when applicable. appliedConfigRevision is the revision the watcher reports running. configYaml is its config file, which can be newer: when pcEditAwaitingRestart is true, the file was edited on the PC while the watcher ran, and that edit takes effect when the watcher restarts.

tools.name: list_watcher_events
tools.title: List Watcher Events
tools.description: Paginated watcher event log (uploads, errors, config sync, update lifecycle). Useful after get_watcher_heartbeats when diagnosing failures.

tools.name: get_watcher_heartbeats
tools.title: Get Watcher Heartbeats
tools.description: Get recent heartbeat history for a watcher agent, useful for diagnosing connectivity gaps and error trends. Returns up to 100 most recent heartbeats within the lookback window.

tools.name: update_watcher_config
tools.title: Update Watcher Config
tools.description: Change a watcher's settings from Data Hub. Admins only. Before calling, call get_watcher, show the user exactly which settings will change (old and new values), and get their confirmation. Pass baseRevision as get_watcher's configRevision. Settings you leave out keep their current values: the pending change if there is one, otherwise the settings the watcher last applied. A rejected change isn't carried over; to retry it, pass its settings again. The change is stored as pending and the watcher applies it within about a minute of its next heartbeat; if the watcher can't (for example the folder doesn't exist), it rejects the change and keeps its old settings. Needs watcher 1.4.0 or later. watch_directory can point at any folder on the instrument PC.

baseRevision.description: The latest revision number from get_watcher (configRevision), or null if it has none. A stale value is refused.

watch_directory.description: Absolute folder on the instrument PC, such as D:\Exports

file_patterns.description: Case-sensitive filename globs, such as *.csv. Replaces the whole list.

pattern.description: Regex with exactly one capture group, matched against the forward-slash path relative to the folder. Group 1 is the run ID.

upload_mode.description: auto uploads new files; manual only reports them until someone requests an upload

tools.name: global_search
tools.title: Global Search
tools.description: Fuzzy search across runs, lab notebooks, files, instruments, users, and comments (same backend as the UI ⌘K palette). Prefer this over search_runs when the query may match a filename, instrument display name, attributor name, user, comment body, or a lab notebook's name or description. A pasted lab notebook link returns only that page's lab notebook, ignoring http vs. https, www., tracking parameters, the fragment, and a Notion page's title. Runs don't match through their notebooks: pass a lab notebook's id to search_runs labNotebookId for its runs, or to get_lab_notebook. The users scope returns workspace member names/emails to any authenticated caller (no row-level member privacy). Use search_runs for date/status/metadata filters. Queries shorter than 2 characters are rejected.

scope.description: Limit results to one entity type (default: all)

url.description: The lab notebook's own page, such as its Notion page.

runCount.description: Live runs in the lab notebook, not held to the result cap. List them with search_runs labNotebookId.

reason.description: Why the instrument is offline. Null in every other state.

connection.description: Whether new files can reach Data Hub. `online`: the watcher checked in within 5 minutes. `restarting`: the watcher stopped for a Windows restart or an automatic update less than 15 minutes ago. `connecting`: the watcher registered and hasn't sent a heartbeat yet, for up to 15 minutes after it registered or the instrument was confirmed; after that the instrument is `offline` with reason `never_checked_in`. `offline`: anything else. This does not take the instrument's status into account: a pending instrument can be `online`.

lastWatcherHeartbeatAt.description: Deprecated. Get the instrument for its `watcher.lastHeartbeatAt`.

tools.name: get_me
tools.title: Get Me
tools.description: Return the authenticated user's identity (id, name, email, image, isAdmin). Use the returned id with search_runs ranBy=, or pass ranBy="me" instead.

tools.name: get_system_status
tools.title: Get System Status
tools.description: Get a dashboard-level overview: per-instrument run counts, whether new files can reach Data Hub (`connection`: online, restarting, connecting, or offline, with a reason when offline), pending upload counts, and how many runs need someone to act (upload failed, failed, or stalled).

runsNeedingAttention.description: Runs whose status needs someone to act: upload_failed, failed, or stalled. Find them with search_runs and that status.

reason.description: Why the instrument is offline. Null in every other state.

connection.description: Whether new files can reach Data Hub. `online`: the watcher checked in within 5 minutes. `restarting`: the watcher stopped for a Windows restart or an automatic update less than 15 minutes ago. `connecting`: the watcher registered and hasn't sent a heartbeat yet, for up to 15 minutes after it registered or the instrument was confirmed; after that the instrument is `offline` with reason `never_checked_in`. `offline`: anything else. This does not take the instrument's status into account: a pending instrument can be `online`.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.title: Search Docs
tools.description: Search Data Hub's own documentation. Use it for how-to and explanation questions about Data Hub itself: setting up instruments and watchers, tokens, permissions, notifications, and MCP and API access. Returns up to five matching sections, each with a short excerpt, a page ID, and a link to cite. Call read_doc to read the full page or section. Not for what changed or when; use search_changelog. Not for lab data; use global_search or search_runs for runs, files, and instruments. When nothing matches, the result lists every docs page so you can pick one. If the results do not answer the question, say the docs do not cover it and offer to report the gap with send_feedback.

query.description: What to look up, as a question or keywords (min 2 characters).

page.description: Page ID to pass to read_doc.

section.description: Heading ID of the matching section, or null for the intro.

pages.description: Every docs page. Present only when nothing matched.

hint.description: Present when no section matches most of the question. Says what to do next.

tools.name: read_doc
tools.title: Read Doc
tools.description: Read one page of Data Hub's documentation as Markdown. Pass a page ID from search_docs, such as `manage-tokens`. Add `section` (a heading ID from the search result) to read only that part. The result lists the page's section IDs, so a long page can be read in pieces. Cite the returned link in your answer. Changelog entries come from search_changelog, not from this tool.

page.description: Page ID from search_docs. A docs path or URL such as /docs/manage-tokens is also accepted.

section.description: Heading ID within the page. Omit to read the whole page.

level.description: 2 for a section, 3 for a subsection.

sections.description: Heading IDs on the page, for reading one section at a time.

tools.name: search_changelog
tools.title: Search Changelog
tools.description: List or search Data Hub's changelog: what changed in the app, the API, the MCP server, and file processing, and when. Use it for "what changed this week", "what's new since October 1", "when did X change", and "is X fixed yet". Leave out `query` to list every entry in a date range, newest first; do not pass "what changed" as the query. With a `query`, the best match comes first. `dateFrom` and `dateTo` are calendar days with both ends included, matched on the day a change was released. A deployment lists an entry only once the change has reached it. Returns whole entries with a link to cite, up to `limit` (default 20, at most 50); `total` says how many matched. Not for how-to questions about using Data Hub; use search_docs. Not for lab data.

query.description: Topic words to look for, such as 'feedback Linear' or 'Hina image preview' (min 2 characters). Leave out to list entries by date alone.

dateFrom.description: First day to include, as YYYY-MM-DD.

dateTo.description: Last day to include, as YYYY-MM-DD.

id.description: Entry ID: the file name without `.md`.

markdown.description: The whole entry as Markdown, without its title.

url.description: Link that opens this entry in Data Hub's changelog. Cite it in your answer.

docsUrl.description: The docs page that explains the change. Null when the entry has none.

total.description: How many entries matched. Larger than `entries` when `limit` cut the list; narrow the dates to see the rest.

hint.description: Present when nothing matched, or no entry clearly matches the query. Says what to do next.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.title: Send Feedback
tools.description: Report a bug or request about Data Hub itself (the web app, MCP tools, or the watcher). Show the user this draft and get their approval before calling. For a problem with a specific run's data, use add_run_comment instead. Any read token can call this.

description.description: What happened or what you want

tools.name: list_feedback
tools.title: List Feedback
tools.description: List feedback reports. Workspace admins see every report, including priority and assignee; everyone else sees only their own, without those. Descriptions longer than 280 characters are shortened. Use get_feedback for the full report and its activity.

status.description: Filter by open, closed, resolved, or declined. closed is resolved and declined together. Results follow Linear's status order, then newest first.

kind.description: Filter by bug, feature_request, or other

tools.name: get_feedback
tools.title: Get Feedback
tools.description: Get one feedback report, including the full description. Admins also get priority, assignee, and the activity list. Pass the report id or the Linear issue ID, such as ENG-1476. Workspace admins can read any report; everyone else can read only their own.

id.description: Feedback report id or Linear issue ID, such as ENG-1476

resources.name: instruments
resources.description: List of all instrument IDs, display names, and types. Use as reference context when constructing tool calls.

resources.name: me
resources.description: Authenticated user's identity (id, name, email, image, isAdmin). Same payload as the get_me tool.

resources.name: glossary
resources.description: Static reference: run status derivation, instrument types, ranBy literals, UTC date semantics, and archive polling.

resources.name: instrument-filter-options
resources.description: Available filter values for an instrument. Values map directly to search_runs metadata filter arguments (wavelength/measurementMode/measurementType for plate readers; captureType/imagingMode/gelWavelength/gelColor for gel-doc; dyeChannel for qPCR; hinaChannel/hinaDimension/hinaSize for Hina; dpi/colorMode for Epson; auntyExperimentType/auntyAnalysisMode/auntyTemperature/auntyRampRate for Aunty).

resources.name: docs-page
resources.description: A page of Data Hub's own documentation as Markdown, such as datahub://docs/manage-tokens. Same text as the read_doc tool. Use search_docs to find the right page.

resources.name: run-report
resources.description: MCP Apps view for a Data Hub instrument run report. Linked from get_run_report.

prompts.name: daily_summary
prompts.title: Daily Summary
prompts.description: Summarize all instrument activity for a given day, including run counts, failures, and system health.

date.description: Date to summarize (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC calendar day). Defaults to the current UTC day.

prompts.name: troubleshoot_instrument
prompts.title: Troubleshoot Instrument
prompts.description: Diagnose connectivity or processing issues for an instrument by inspecting its status and watcher health.

prompts.name: compare_runs
prompts.title: Compare Runs
prompts.description: Compare the results of two runs side by side, highlighting differences in experimental outcomes.

instrumentId.description: Instrument identifier (both runs must be on the same instrument)

prompts.name: find_my_runs
prompts.title: Find My Runs
prompts.description: List runs claimed by the authenticated user, optionally scoped to an instrument and date range.

prompts.name: explain_failed_run
prompts.title: Explain Failed Run
prompts.description: Diagnose why a run failed and suggest reprocess or upload fixes.

prompts.name: claim_unattributed_runs
prompts.title: Claim Unattributed Runs
prompts.description: Find unattributed runs on an instrument and claim them for the authenticated user after confirmation.

prompts.name: summarize_instrument_week
prompts.title: Summarize Instrument Week
prompts.description: Summarize one instrument's activity over the last seven days (or a provided window).

dateFrom.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Defaults to 7 days ago (UTC).

dateTo.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC). Defaults to today (UTC).
